# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

blocks.text:
name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

 - `validation_failed` — sticky guest park (owner 2026-09-27, live: fa#923 — a guest PR cycled arm→CI red→silent-update→re-arm every tick, holding the validate-armed limit-1 slot hostage). The silent-update action sets it on a GUEST PR whose current head has red checks; while it is set the PR is excluded from the validate-armed arm queue and NO validation CI is dispatched for it at all. It is removed only when the head's last committer is NOT `sm-silent-update` — i.e. an author push; the SM's own silent-update merges never clear it. Machine-authored PRs never carry the label (their heads are pushed by the machine; they re-enter validation on a new head as usual).
 
+
+## Merge-window cadence (gh-837)
+
+The post-approval window is strictly serial by default: one `ai_validating` arm at a time (`mutex` + `mutexAmong [pr_approved]`), so each merge pays a BEHIND refresh (~10–15 min) plus a full validation CI (~30–40 min) — a ~45–60 min/merge ceiling (owner expectation: 1 merge / 30 min, floor 1/hour).
+
+`jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default **1** — unchanged legacy behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the arm mutex to N concurrent approved validations **when the approved queue depth is at/above** `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). With the knob active the SM also patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate recovery twins and raises the arm limit to the cap, so every free slot fills in one tick: the parallel validations conclude together and the mergeBot's one-run batch (it merges every green + CLEAN approved head per run) lands them in a single window. L2 replay (`js/unit-tests/test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge.
+
+Runner cost stays hard-capped at N × `validationMinutesEstimate` (default 35) validation-minutes per tick and is reported on the tick log (and the action result's `validationCost` field). A red validation still parks exactly one head — fail-validation is per-PR and the parallel arms share no state (#832 semantics preserved); the dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]` scope) is untouched.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. ## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

Now let me review the key logic concerns:

1. **githubSource.js mutexMax logic (exclude-self branch)**: 
```js
var blocked = !selfHolds && otherHolders >= mutexMax;
```
Previously: `blocked = !selfHolds && items.some(other holds)`. With mutexMax=1, `otherHolders >= 1` — same as before. Good.

But wait — there's a subtlety: `holders` is computed from `items` before filtering. In the exclude-self branch, `items` includes the candidates themselves (self-holders). The candidates that are processed — `holders` filter uses `holdsMutex` which checks if item has the mutex label. But `items` at this point: what is `items`? It's the query result items. In the non-exclude-self branch, `holders.length >= mutexMax` — previously `items.some(holdsMutex)`. Same for mutexMax=1. Good backward compat.

One issue: in the exclude-self branch, the candidate filtering previously used `items.some(...)` — `items` is the unfiltered list. Now `holders` is the same list filtered. For the candidate counting `holders[hi] !== candidate && holders[hi].prNumber !== candidate.prNumber` — double condition, fine.

2. **validationMutexHeldByAnother in smAgent.js**: `return otherHolders >= mutexMax ? firstOtherHolder : 0;` — previously `return otherHolder` (first other holder number or 0). With mutexMax=1: otherHolders >= 1 → returns firstOtherHolder. Same. Good.

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. - **Author**: ai-teammate

- **Additions**: +869
- **Deletions**: -19

- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T11:00:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 2411 passed, 0 failed

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

blocks.text:
name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

@@ -21,6 +21,15 @@ The machine's state lives in labels; two are owner-facing semantics worth knowin
 - `blocked` — human hold: the item is invisible to EVERY rule (all legs) until a human removes the label.
 - `validation_failed` — sticky guest park (owner 2026-09-27, live: fa#923 — a guest PR cycled arm→CI red→silent-update→re-arm every tick, holding the validate-armed limit-1 slot hostage). The silent-update action sets it on a GUEST PR whose current head has red checks; while it is set the PR is excluded from the validate-armed arm queue and NO validation CI is dispatched for it at all. It is removed only when the head's last committer is NOT `sm-silent-update` — i.e. an author push; the SM's own silent-update merges never clear it. Machine-authored PRs never carry the label (their heads are pushed by the machine; they re-enter validation on a new head as usual).
 
+
+## Merge-window cadence (gh-837)
+
+The post-approval window is strictly serial by default: one `ai_validating` arm at a time (`mutex` + `mutexAmong [pr_approved]`), so each merge pays a BEHIND refresh (~10–15 min) plus a full validation CI (~30–40 min) — a ~45–60 min/merge ceiling (owner expectation: 1 merge / 30 min, floor 1/hour).
+
+`jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default **1** — unchanged legacy behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the arm mutex to N concurrent approved validations **when the approved queue depth is at/above** `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). With the knob active the SM also patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate recovery twins and raises the arm limit to the cap, so every free slot fills in one tick: the parallel validations conclude together and the mergeBot's one-run batch (it merges every green + CLEAN approved head per run) lands them in a single window. L2 replay (`js/unit-tests/test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge.
+
+Runner cost stays hard-capped at N × `validationMinutesEstimate` (default 35) validation-minutes per tick and is reported on the tick log (and the action result's `validationCost` field). A red validation still parks exactly one head — fail-validation is per-PR and the parallel arms share no state (#832 semantics preserved); the dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]` scope) is untouched.
+

Read input context:

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. - **Author**: ai-teammate

- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T11:00:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 2411 passed, 0 failed
```

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

 - `validation_failed` — sticky guest park (owner 2026-09-27, live: fa#923 — a guest PR cycled arm→CI red→silent-update→re-arm every tick, holding the validate-armed limit-1 slot hostage). The silent-update action sets it on a GUEST PR whose current head has red checks; while it is set the PR is excluded from the validate-armed arm queue and NO validation CI is dispatched for it at all. It is removed only when the head's last committer is NOT `sm-silent-update` — i.e. an author push; the SM's own silent-update merges never clear it. Machine-authored PRs never carry the label (their heads are pushed by the machine; they re-enter validation on a new head as usual).
 
+
+## Merge-window cadence (gh-837)
+
+The post-approval window is strictly serial by default: one `ai_validating` arm at a time (`mutex` + `mutexAmong [pr_approved]`), so each merge pays a BEHIND refresh (~10–15 min) plus a full validation CI (~30–40 min) — a ~45–60 min/merge ceiling (owner expectation: 1 merge / 30 min, floor 1/hour).
+
+`jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default **1** — unchanged legacy behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the arm mutex to N concurrent approved validations **when the approved queue depth is at/above** `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). With the knob active the SM also patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate recovery twins and raises the arm limit to the cap, so every free slot fills in one tick: the parallel validations conclude together and the mergeBot's one-run batch (it merges every green + CLEAN approved head per run) lands them in a single window. L2 replay (`js/unit-tests/test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge.
+
+Runner cost stays hard-capped at N × `validationMinutesEstimate` (default 35) validation-minutes per tick and is reported on the tick log (and the action result's `validationCost` field). A red validation still parks exactly one head — fail-validation is per-PR and the parallel arms share no state (#832 semantics preserved); the dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]` scope) is untouched.

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 838
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/838
- **Title**: gh-837 [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min parallel validation or merge-train needed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-837` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +869
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T11:00:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T11:00:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 2411 passed, 0 failed

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-837` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +869
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T11:00:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T11:00:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 2411 passed, 0 failed
```

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

 - `blocked` — human hold: the item is invisible to EVERY rule (all legs) until a human removes the label.
 - `validation_failed` — sticky guest park (owner 2026-09-27, live: fa#923 — a guest PR cycled arm→CI red→silent-update→re-arm every tick, holding the validate-armed limit-1 slot hostage). The silent-update action sets it on a GUEST PR whose current head has red checks; while it is set the PR is excluded from the validate-armed arm queue and NO validation CI is dispatched for it at all. It is removed only when the head's last committer is NOT `sm-silent-update` — i.e. an author push; the SM's own silent-update merges never clear it. Machine-authored PRs never carry the label (their heads are pushed by the machine; they re-enter validation on a new head as usual).
 
+
+## Merge-window cadence (gh-837)
+
+The post-approval window is strictly serial by default: one `ai_validating` arm at a time (`mutex` + `mutexAmong [pr_approved]`), so each merge pays a BEHIND refresh (~10–15 min) plus a full validation CI (~30–40 min) — a ~45–60 min/merge ceiling (owner expectation: 1 merge / 30 min, floor 1/hour).
+
+`jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default **1** — unchanged legacy behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the arm mutex to N concurrent approved validations **when the approved queue depth is at/above** `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). With the knob active the SM also patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate recovery twins and raises the arm limit to the cap, so every free slot fills in one tick: the parallel validations conclude together and the mergeBot's one-run batch (it merges every green + CLEAN approved head per run) lands them in a single window. L2 replay (`js/unit-tests/test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge.
+
+Runner cost stays hard-capped at N × `validationMinutesEstimate` (default 35) validation-minutes per tick and is reported on the tick log (and the action result's `validationCost` field). A red validation still parks exactly one head — fail-validation is per-PR and the parallel arms share no state (#832 semantics preserved); the dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]` scope) is untouched.

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

### How to verify

dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 2411 passed, 0 failed
