Tool error (bash): # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. +
+The post-approval window is strictly serial by default: one `ai_validating` arm at a time (`mutex` + `mutexAmong [pr_approved]`), so each merge pays a BEHIND refresh (~10–15 min) plus a full validation CI (~30–40 min) — a ~45–60 min/merge ceiling (owner expectation: 1 merge / 30 min, floor 1/hour).

Tool error (bash): # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

blocks.text:
Tool error (bash): # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 838
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/838
- **Title**: gh-837 [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min parallel validation or merge-train needed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-837` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +957
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T11:00:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T11:28:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 2411 passed, 0 failed
```

2. **The `pick` warn condition**: `if (typeof cfgVal !== 'undefined' && cfgVal !== null)` — after parsing strings, if cfgVal was `'abc'`, parseInt gives NaN; `normalizePositiveInt(NaN)` → probably null → warn. OK.

3. **`approvedQueueDepth` fail-closed to 0** — good. But note: it counts `pr_approved` non-blocked non-draft PRs — including ones that hold `ai_validating` (the description says "approved queue depth"). Watermark semantics fine.

4. **The patch only applies when `validationConcurrencyCfg.max > 1`** — even when below watermark, no patch — so mutexMax stays absent → serial. Good.

5. **A subtle issue in the patch condition**: rules are matched by `q.mutex === 'ai_validating' && q.mutexAmong includes 'pr_approved'`. But `applyRuleOverrides` runs earlier (line 5300) — if projectConfig.smRuleOverrides patch these rules, the patch here runs after, fine.

6. **Priority sort + raised limit**: with limit raised to N, the preemption marker `keptCount = Math.min(limit, matched.length)` now computes with the raised limit — fine.

7. **`reportValidationCost`** duplicates the filtering logic twice (slotsInUse and depth) — could be a single pass. Minor duplication: labels mapping repeated. It's a SUGGESTION-level nit.

9. **Potential issue — the twins' `mutexMax` patch**: The patch applies `mutexMax` to ALL rules with mutex ai_validating among pr_approved, including the exclude-self twins. In githubSource exclude-self form, mutexMax only affects NON-holders (self-holders always drain). For a non-holder candidate arming when holders=1, mutexMax=2 → returns 0 → proceeds. Good.

Tool error (bash): # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

- **Title**: gh-837 [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min parallel validation or merge-train needed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-837` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +957
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T11:00:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T11:28:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 2411 passed, 0 failed
```

blocks.text:
Tool error (bash): # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 838
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/838
- **Title**: gh-837 [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min parallel validation or merge-train needed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-837` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +957
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T11:00:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T11:28:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 2411 passed, 0 failed
```

Tool error (bash): # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

Tool error (bash): # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 838
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/838
- **Title**: gh-837 [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min parallel validation or merge-train needed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-837` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +957
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T11:00:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T11:28:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 2411 passed, 0 failed
```

blocks.text:
Tool error (bash): # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 838
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/838
- **Title**: gh-837 [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min parallel validation or merge-train needed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-837` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +957
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T11:00:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T11:28:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 2411 passed, 0 failed
```

All relevant tests pass. Now let me do a deep review of the logic for correctness issues:

1. **`resolveValidationConcurrency` `pick()` logic**: The `pick` function takes cfg first, then json. But there's a subtle bug-ish behavior: if `cfgVal` is a valid positive int it returns; if cfgVal is defined but invalid → warn; then falls to jsonVal. Looks right.

But wait — `normalizePositiveInt` — check what it does. If it clamps 0/negative to null. Fine.

2. **The `pick` warn condition**: `if (typeof cfgVal !== 'undefined' && cfgVal !== null)` — after parsing strings, if cfgVal was `'abc'`, parseInt gives NaN; `normalizePositiveInt(NaN)` → probably null → warn. OK.

3. **`approvedQueueDepth` fail-closed to 0** — good. But note: it counts `pr_approved` non-blocked non-draft PRs — including ones that hold `ai_validating` (the description says "approved queue depth"). Watermark semantics fine.

4. **The patch only applies when `validationConcurrencyCfg.max > 1`** — even when below watermark, no patch — so mutexMax stays absent → serial. Good.

5. **A subtle issue in the patch condition**: rules are matched by `q.mutex === 'ai_validating' && q.mutexAmong includes 'pr_approved'`. But `applyRuleOverrides` runs earlier (line 5300) — if projectConfig.smRuleOverrides patch these rules, the patch here runs after, fine.

6. **Priority sort + raised limit**: with limit raised to N, the preemption marker `keptCount = Math.min(limit, matched.length)` now computes with the raised limit — fine.

7. **`reportValidationCost`** duplicates the filtering logic twice (slotsInUse and depth) — could be a single pass. Minor duplication: labels mapping repeated. It's a SUGGESTION-level nit.

8. **Watermark probe and rule-guard mismatch**: `approvedQueueDepth` counts pr_approved non-draft non-blocked. The `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` default 3. OK.

9. **Potential issue — the twins' `mutexMax` patch**: The patch applies `mutexMax` to ALL rules with mutex ai_validating among pr_approved, including the exclude-self twins. In githubSource exclude-self form, mutexMax only affects NON-holders (self-holders always drain). The twins don't arm new PRs (they re-dispatch CI on already-armed PRs), so `mutexMax` for them only gates whether a NON-holder matches — the twins' queries require labels ['pr_approved','ai_validating'] so candidates are holders anyway... Actually a candidate could be pr_approved+ai_validating = self-holds. So the mutexMax for twins is effectively inert (all candidates self-hold). Harmless but the description in sm_github.json says "non-holder defers only once OTHER approved arms reach the cap" — consistent.

Wait — actually there's a subtlety: with exclude-self and mutexMax=N, a non-holder candidate defers when otherHolders >= N. For the twins, candidates always carry ai_validating (query labels include it), so they self-hold. Inert. Fine.

10. **Limit raising only on `typeof rule.limit === 'number'`** — validate-armed has limit 1. Good.

11. **Race within a tick when arming N**: validate-armed's localAction 'validate_pr' does the action-time mutex re-check `validationMutexHeldByAnother` per candidate against a LIVE list (dropOpenPrsCache'd). Both arms in one tick: first arm adds ai_validating to pr-2, drops cache; second candidate pr-3 re-check sees 1 other holder (< 2) → proceeds. Good.

12. **A real potential BUG — `validationMutexHeldByAnother` counting self-holding candidates for the global (non-exclude-self) form**: In the global form, `q.mutexExcludeSelf` is falsy. The re-check: `if (q.mutexExcludeSelf && selfHolds) return 0;` then `return otherHolders >= mutexMax ? firstOtherHolder : 0`. For a non-holder candidate arming when holders=1, mutexMax=2 → returns 0 → proceeds. Good.

13. **mergeBot batch merge assumption**: The cadence claim rests on mergeBot merging every green CLEAN approved head per run. That's an external component; the PR didn't change it. The sim models it. OK — noted as an assumption; AC4 live soak covers it.

14. **Documentation/CI**: the docs-freshness failure is the one BLOCKING. The fix: regenerate and commit `docs/agents/generated/sm_github.md`.

15. Another check — the comment in smAgent.js header says ".dmtools/config.js smValidationConcurrency overrides, clamped to 5". `resolveValidationConcurrency` clamps the RESOLVED max to 5 regardless of source. OK.

16. **`effectiveValidationConcurrency(cfg, approvedDepth)`** — `approvedDepth >= cfg.watermark`. If watermark resolves to huge number, stays serial. Fine.

Tool error (bash): # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

- **Title**: gh-837 [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min parallel validation or merge-train needed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-837` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +957
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T11:00:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T11:28:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 2411 passed, 0 failed
```

Tool error (bash): # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 838
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/838
- **Title**: gh-837 [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min parallel validation or merge-train needed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-837` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +957
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T11:00:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T11:28:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 2411 passed, 0 failed
```

In githubSource exclude-self form, mutexMax only affects NON-holders (self-holders always drain). The twins don't arm new PRs (they re-dispatch CI on already-armed PRs), so `mutexMax` for them only gates whether a NON-holder matches — the twins' queries require labels ['pr_approved','ai_validating'] so candidates are holders anyway... Tool error (bash): # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).
